what: the concave half circle where a block as wide as the cylinder's diameter meets the cylinder's wall above its top, rounded r2 with its tangent chain: the half circle's pieces, ending where it runs on into the block's convex top-side edges
method: block 40x20x15 (x 0..40, y -10..10) joined to the cylinder R10 x 30 on the z axis: the block's sides y = +-10 run tangent into the cylinder wall at x = 0; V0 = 12000 + 3000 pi - 15 * 50 pi = 19068.5835. The arc (z = 15, rho = 10, x > 0) ends at (0, +-10, 15), where the block's top-side edges go on tangentially. Rounded r2 with its tangent chain: SMLib splits the half circle, and the chain takes every piece of it (concave, tangent at their ends); at (0, +-10, 15) it runs on into convex edges, where a chain ends (a round cannot pass from one side of the faces to the other), so the half circle is rounded whole and alone; the round adds the spandrel (rho in [10,12], z in [15,17]) over the block only, between its side planes |y| = 10: at radius rho it spans 2 asin(10/rho), running out to nothing at the ends. Added = int over the spandrel of 2 rho asin(10/rho) (Gauss-Legendre) = 23.3785. V = 19091.9620.
